newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico farm chief sees few grain imports to yr end.
newsitem.headline: Mexico farm chief sees few grain imports to yr end.

text.p: Mexico will only import marginal amounts of grains, and probably no corn, to the year end, one of the top private sector farm leaders said Monday.

Miguel Castro, chairman of the National Farming Council, told reporters that because of recent rains across much of the country, chances for a recovery of the spring-summer harvest have increased lessening the need to import.
"I only see marginal amounts of grains being imported to the end of the year, Chavez said. "For corn, for this year, now we do not need imports," Chavez said.

Chavez said the original estimates of Mexico probably needing to import around 8 million tonnes of grains are coming down because of the rains. He said the total grain import need would be around 4 million tonnes for 1996.

But that revised estimate appears to be on the low side despite the rosier outlook for the upcoming harvest. Government reports obtained by Reuters have the January-June imports of corn at 3.5 million tonnes, without considering other grains.
Castro said soybeans were the one exception to the import forecast to the end of 1996. "We are going to import around 1 million tonnes of soybeans in 1996," he said.

That figure too is well down on the 2,229,188 tonnes imported in 1995, according to Agriculture Ministry figures. It is also much lower than the 2.3 million tonne import estimate for 1996 from the Mexico City office of the American Soybean Association.
